jobs.title: Research Technician (Nights / Weekends)
jobs.description_text: ABOUT ALLJOINED Alljoined is creating a future where humans are fully understood and augmented by technology. Our work solves the communication bottleneck between humans and computers by decoding thoughts from the brain, entirely non-invasively. We apply deep learning research to large scale EEG datasets to decode multimedia input, eventually moving to internal thought. We are state-of-the art in capabilities and are fully vertically integrated. Our goal is to develop a general consumer interface to completely transform how we can live our lives. We are actively growing our world-class team of researchers to build the next interface to improve individual lives as well as the well-being of society as a whole. ABOUT THE ROLE As a Research Technician, you will work directly with research participants running neural data collection sessions with precision and care while ensuring our datasets meet the quality standards required for cutting-edge deep research. Responsibilities include setting up participants, configuring experiments, monitoring live signal quality, troubleshooting software and hardware issues, and handing off clean sessions and clear communication to the team. You will work hands-on with hardware and experimental workflows, sitting at the intersection of human interaction and high-throughput data collection - directly enabling the neural decoding breakthroughs our team is pursuing. Our pioneering work in human computation, synthetic data, simulation and RL give us the advantage in delivering results to our customers. Why now? What happens if we succeed? Abundant will be the core enabler for not only AGI, but ASI and physical intelligence. Most of the challenges in model algorithms and compute are already solved. jobs.title: Expression of Interest
jobs.description_text: Aptura is an applied AI research company. We work with frontier AI labs to improve how their models handle complex, real-world professional work in finance, legal, healthcare, policy and beyond. We do it by working with experienced practitioners who create versions of real work: the models, documents, presentations and analyses that show AI what good actually looks like. The shape of the work - Paid project work that is designed to run alongside full-time employment. - Remote and asynchronous: you pick up discrete tasks and are paid per completed task - Scope, fee, deadlines and payment terms are confirmed individually in writing before you start - Your work is reviewed by senior professionals from your own field What you might build Depending on your background: financial models and investment presentations; legal drafting or document review; clinical and scientific analysis; policy briefs; or expert review of other contributors' work. Who we're looking for People who have personally owned real work - you can describe what you built, who it was for, and what made it hard. We care about judgment over retrieval, and we value people who work well asynchronously and take feedback seriously. What happens next We review your expression of interest and, where there's a potential fit, arrange a short call to discuss your experience, capacity and terms - then match you to a live project.

jobs.title: Associate Red Team Analyst - Mexico
jobs.description_text: Role Overview A successful Associate Red Team Analyst at Armadin should possess an understanding of both offensive information security and artificial intelligence workflows. They should understand fundamental concepts such as web application architecture, authentication mechanisms, and network security, and be able to learn advanced concepts such as AI safety constraints, attacker data classification, and context-driven exploit validation. This is not a traditional "monitor the dashboard" defensive SOC job; this career is technical, offensive-focused, and challenging, with opportunities to work at the cutting edge of AI-driven red teaming alongside world-class red teamers. A typical shift could involve reviewing an AI attacker's safety disengagement during a complex web application test, bypassing a sophisticated CAPTCHA to unblock an automated attack path, or providing the missing contextual judgment an AI needs to exploit a deep vulnerability. If you can rapidly evaluate applications, make critical safety judgments on the fly, think like a red teamer, and feed data back to engineering teams to improve AI models, then you’re the type of analyst we’re looking for. As an Armadin Red Team Analyst, you’ll get hands-on experience acting as the "human-in-the-loop" for complex security problems on a daily basis. jobs.description_text: Role Overview Every operator knows the ending. You found the path, chained it to access the crown jewel, and wrote it up. Then the engagement closed, the environment changed the next week, and nobody walked that kill chain again until next year's test. Armadin is built to end that cycle. We're building an agentic attacker swarm. These are specialized AI agents running custom models that discover, exploit, and chain vulnerabilities across external, internal, identity, cloud, and application attack surfaces. They run continuously, at machine speed, against live production environments. Until recently, nobody could put a nation-state-caliber adversary inside every network around the clock. That's the hyperattack, and it's what we do. In one recent engagement, the swarm generated more than 17 million offensive actions in three days and validated 38 attack paths. That's the scale your tradecraft will run at. As a Principal Red Team Operator, your tradecraft is the training signal. You'll run hands-on operations, and then you'll encode how you think into the reasoning our agents use at scale: how you pick a foothold, abuse an application's logic, pivot through identity, separate what's actually exploitable from scanner noise, and map the blast radius once you're in. jobs.description_text: ABOUT ASTERA: Astera is a private foundation on a mission to steer science and technology toward a better future. ABOUT PRISM: Prism is making protein motion measurable, predictable, and actionable. Proteins are always moving, and that movement drives their function: binding, catalysis, allostery, selectivity, and mutational effects all emerge from conformational ensembles, the distribution of states a protein moves between. Yet most structural data rests on static snapshots that capture form, not function, because motion has been hard to measure and interpret. As a result, we lack critical levers to correct proteins in disease and engineer them for new purposes. Prism is building open, usable tools, methods, and infrastructure to study protein dynamics from experimental data, and applying them to pressing biological questions, including binding affinity, enzyme engineering, and explaining pathogenic variants. Prism sits with Radial, Astera’s Life Sciences Division. ABOUT RADIAL: Radial is Astera's life sciences division. We tackle foundational problems in biology while simultaneously prototyping better ways to fund, organize, and share research. Radial builds programs in-house, funds external teams, and designs partnerships in service of public-good science. COMPANY OVERVIEW Astera Neuro seeks to understand and engineer consciousness. We believe consciousness is the process by which the brain builds a coherent internal model of the world and the self. We aim to understand this model and to develop the technologies to write experience directly into the brain. By combining large-scale neural recording, causal perturbation, and brain-based AI, we seek to move neuroscience from observing correlates of experience to engineering it. The same tools carry direct therapeutic promise for neurological and psychiatric diseases that alter perception, thought, and sense of self. Because the science and tools required do not yet exist, we are assembling a founding team of neuroscientists, theorists, and engineers to create them. As a company at the forefront of space exploration and satellite technology, Apex is looking for an individual capable of owning complex projects and serving as the primary liaison between our internal teams and launch providers while also leading launch campaigns. The Launch Engineer is also responsible for setting up companywide processes to ensure our vehicles launch reliably. **Note** We are open to considering candidates across multiple levels, so if this opportunity interests you but the posted range does not fully align with your expectations, we still encourage you to apply Responsibilities: - Manage and coordinate the integration of satellite payloads with various launch vehicles. - Work closely with launch providers to define mission requirements, interfaces, and integration schedules. - Develop and maintain satellite launch plans, procedures, and readiness reviews. - Oversee satellite transportation, handling, and pre-launch processing at launch sites. - Ensure compatibility between the satellite and launch vehicle, including mechanical, electrical, and environmental interfaces. - Support environmental testing (vibration, thermal vacuum, EMI/EMC) to validate satellite launch readiness. - Conduct system-level checkouts and troubleshooting during pre-launch and countdown operations. - Interface with regulatory agencies to secure launch approvals and compliance

jobs.title: Senior Spacecraft GNC Engineer
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking a seasoned Senior Spacecraft GNC Engineer to work on a closely integrated team who will drive the design of the GNC system, including hardware and software, to meet the position, attitude, knowledge and stability requirements of our bus. You will have an opportunity to approach this from a clean sheet design and inform coupled trades across the vehicle architecture. You will be innovative in your approach to push the limits of design and performance, while disrupting and making an impact on the industry. This role reports directly into the Director of GNC, HITL & Mission Ops. Responsibilities: - Develop and implement GNC algorithms for satellite systems, including attitude determination and control, orbit determination and control, and precision pointing. - Conduct analysis of spacecraft dynamics and perform simulations to evaluate system performance, stability, and accuracy. - Design, develop, and test spacecraft control systems, including reaction wheels, thrusters, and magnetic torquers, to achieve desired mission objectives. - Collaborate with spacecraft and payload engineers to define system requirements and ensure GNC system compatibility and integration. - Perform trade studies and make recommendations for optimal GNC configurations, considering factors such as power consumption, mass, and cost. - Develop and execute test plans and procedures for GNC systems, including system-level testing, performance evaluation, and anomaly resolution. -

jobs.title: Red Team Engineer, Product Security
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE As our Red Team Engineer, you will attack our own products the way a capable adversary would: spacecraft, ground stations, cloud command-and-control software, and the pipelines and factory processes that produce them. You will run our internal assessments, lead the outside firms we bring in, build testing tools that keep up the pressure between assessments, and bring an attacker's perspective into design reviews while there is still time to change the design. This is a hands-on engineering role, not an audit, compliance, or security policy role. ABOUT THE TEAM Apex builds spacecraft, the flight software that runs them, the ground systems and cloud software used to command them, and the test equipment and emulators used to develop them. In this industry a security failure can cost an entire mission, so we try to find the weaknesses before anyone else does. Product Security is a small team with a big footprint. You would be its second core member, working directly with the Product Security Architect and alongside security engineers embedded in our flight software, ground software, and development infrastructure teams. This role plays a critical part in protecting classified and sensitive data in AWS, Azure, and hybrid/multi-cloud infrastructures while ensuring full compliance with federal standards such as NIST 800-53, FedRAMP, RMF, and DoD Impact Levels (IL-4/IL-5). The right candidate will bring hands-on experience securing cloud platforms in regulated environments. This role will help the organization meet industry standards such as SOC2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, GDPR/CCPA, or other relevant compliance frameworks. Experience in the space industry is not necessary to thrive at Apex. Instead, we are looking for motivated engineers who enjoy solving complex problems, balance technical rigor with practicality, and thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. The Flight Software team is composed of three interconnected teams: high-level application software, operating system software, and embedded software. There is significant collaboration and crossover across these teams. This role is highly hands-on while also providing technical guidance, mentorship, and day-to-day coordination for the solar production team. Responsibilities: - Lead day-to-day assembly, integration, and testing of spacecraft solar arrays. - Mentor and train technicians while coordinating build priorities, task assignments, and progress. - Perform and oversee solar array assembly, including mechanical fastening, bonding, composites, wiring, harnessing, and precision alignment. - Support integration of solar cells, electrical systems, composite structures, and deployment hardware. - Perform and oversee electrical and functional testing, including continuity checks and troubleshooting. - Support environmental and deployment testing of flight hardware. - Lead troubleshooting and root-cause analysis alongside engineering and quality. - Identify and escalate build issues, nonconformances, and production blockers. - Ensure builds meet engineering drawings, work instructions, quality standards, and safety requirements. - Maintain accurate build documentation, inspection records, and test results. - Partner with engineering to improve tooling, fixtures, processes, and work instructions. - Drive continuous improvement in production efficiency, quality, and repeatability as solar array production scales. Requirements: - U.S. Person status

jobs.title: Propulsion Engineer, Structures (Mid)
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Apex is seeking a Propulsion Engineer with experience in structures and hardware integration to design the propulsion modules that bolt onto Apex spacecraft at scale. You will own mechanical designs across the module, including the structure, mounting and installation of flow controllers, PPUs, and thrusters, and the packaging that turns a set of components into a single, buildable, flight-ready assembly. What makes this role distinctive is that the propulsion components you're integrating are designed and built in-house at Apex. You'll work directly with the engineers who own our thrusters, cathodes, flow controllers, and PPUs, helping shape their mechanical, thermal, and interface design so the components and module are optimized together from the start. You'll also work closely with our manufacturing team throughout the design cycle, supporting first builds and incorporating feedback from the production floor as we scale. This role offers significant hands-on design ownership and the opportunity to take hardware from concept through build, test, and production. Your team will also own spacecraft propellant servicing, including fill and drain operations, ground support equipment, procedures, and range compliance. You will work closely with our mission operations, GNC, and hardware teams to architect new systems, prototype ideas, and turn them into mission-critical software that ultimately flies. Experience in the space industry is not necessary to thrive at Apex. Instead, we are looking for motivated engineers who enjoy solving complex problems, balance technical rigor with practicality, and thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. The Flight Software team is composed of three interconnected teams: high-level application software, operating system software, and embedded software. There is significant collaboration and crossover across these teams. Baseten owns the entire pipeline, from the moment a developer pushes a model to the moment a request gets a response. That vertical ownership means we can fix these problems at the root. jobs.title: Software Engineer - Compute and Isolation
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Every agent on Baseten Sandboxes gets its own microVM, where it writes and runs code, calls tools, and keeps state across long tasks. Agents pause and resume constantly, so the machine underneath has to start, stop, snapshot, fork, and resume fast, and keep every tenant isolated while it does. General-purpose virtualization was not built for that workload. The Agent Infra team builds that layer. Sandboxes run in microVMs with custom Linux kernels on bare-metal servers we operate. You'll own how sandboxes start, stop, snapshot, fork, and resume, and how they perform on each host's CPU and memory, down to the hardware. You'll also own the guest and host side of each sandbox: its identity, how it attaches to different storage classes for performance or capabilities, and the virtual devices that connect it securely to the network. In September 2026, Baseten acquired Blaxel https://www.baseten.co/blog/blaxel-is-joining-baseten-to-build-the-future-of-agentic-cloud/, whose microVM sandboxes are the foundation for Baseten Sandboxes https://docs.baseten.co/sandboxes. We are building a cloud, not just using one. That means designing for many tenants from day one and thinking through what each decision means all the way down to the datacenter. The team is small and ownership is big: we ship in weeks and months, not multi-year programs. jobs.title: Software Engineer - Networking (Agent Infra)
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Every agent on Baseten Sandboxes runs in its own microVM. Agents call models, reach tools and APIs, expose services, and more and more often talk to each other. Networking built into today's cloud providers was not designed for very large numbers of isolated machines that suspend, resume, and exchange data constantly. The Agent Infra team builds its own networking stack for sandboxes, designed from the start for that scale. It runs in user space, with VPP (FD.io http://FD.io) as its main data plane technology, and is built from virtualized network functions (VNF/NFV): carrier-grade, low-latency packet processing designed for very large numbers of agents. In September 2026, Baseten acquired Blaxel https://www.baseten.co/blog/blaxel-is-joining-baseten-to-build-the-future-of-agentic-cloud/, whose sandboxes, storage, and networking are the foundation for Baseten Sandboxes https://docs.baseten.co/sandboxes. You'll build multi-tenant virtual private networking that connects each customer's agents and services privately and securely, using modern overlay technologies. We are building a cloud, not just using one. We want engineers who expose the network as a programmable API and write the code, not operators who push router and switch configuration. The team is small and ownership is big: we ship in weeks and months, not multi-year programs. This role is separate from Baseten's GPU-to-GPU networking. jobs.title: Software Engineer - Storage Systems (Agent Infra)
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Storage decides how fast agent sandboxes start and how safely they share data. Agents need a filesystem that thousands of sandboxes mount at the same time, with strict isolation and the consistency agents need. Agent context is mostly small files, so the access patterns look very different from storage built for large files. The Agent Infra team builds Agent Drive, the distributed filesystem that agent sandboxes mount over FUSE, and the storage underneath it. The work uses tiered caching, replication, content-addressed data, and Linux filesystem internals. In September 2026, Baseten acquired Blaxel https://www.baseten.co/blog/blaxel-is-joining-baseten-to-build-the-future-of-agentic-cloud/, whose sandboxes and Agent Drive filesystem are the foundation for Baseten Sandboxes https://docs.baseten.co/sandboxes. We are building a cloud, not just using one, so storage is designed for many tenants from day one. The team is small and ownership is big: we ship in weeks and months, not multi-year programs. If you care about page cache coherency, FUSE, replication protocols, and content-addressable storage, we'd love to talk. jobs.title: Manager / Senior Manager, Global Regulatory Affairs, Lifecycle Management (Los Altos)
jobs.description_text: "Bring hands-on regulatory judgment to AI that runs the registered life of a product." ■ About Cheiron Cheiron is building AI software for regulatory lifecycle management in the pharmaceutical industry, and we are working with our first pilot customers. The platform keeps track of what is registered in each market (the approved state, commitments and conditions, and the filings needed to keep registrations current) and, when a manufacturing or quality change is proposed, works out what it means in each market for review by qualified regulatory staff. It also drafts and checks regulatory documents. Customers keep their own regulatory records, and their qualified staff make the formal decisions; Cheiron supports that work. ■ About the Role You will work alongside AI that produces first drafts, assessments and checks. Your judgment decides what is right, and your work makes the system better. You will be the hands-on global regulatory affairs expert on a growing Life Sciences team, responsible for regulatory correctness across the registered life of a product, from routine maintenance to the cases the guidelines do not settle. You own the work for your assigned accounts within agreed scopes. Our Associate Director of Regulatory Affairs is the team's senior regulatory authority: you document hard cases, propose a position and escalate, and the Associate Director makes the final call.
